diagnosis:
The gauge sits at the outlet of Lake Vyrnwy, a reservoir that supplies Liverpool. Observed flow averages about 2.2 mm/day while precipitation averages 5.4 mm/day and PET only 1.3 mm/day. Much of the water is therefore abstracted, and standard HBV cannot remove it through evapotranspiration. The default parameters overestimated flow by 88% (NSE -0.70).

To make the model lose water at a steady rate, I fixed K2 at about 1e-6, so water percolating to the lower zone (PERC about 2 mm/day) effectively leaves the system. A large FC (about 500 mm, at its upper search bound), a low LP and a slow upper zone (K1 about 0.013, UZL about 190) produce the damped, seasonal response of a reservoir that fills in autumn before spilling.

Calibration (DDS on NSE, 1971–1997): NSE 0.63, KGE 0.75, bias -5.5%. With the same parameters, 1987–1997 alone gives NSE 0.66 with near-zero bias. Recalibrating on 1987–1997 raised that period's NSE only to 0.67 with similar parameters, which suggests the calibration holds steady over time.

Weak points: compensation-flow baseflow, the timing of reservoir spills, and summer droughts are all managed operations, not natural rainfall-runoff, so peaks and recessions are only partly captured. The individual parameters have no physical meaning, and FC sits at its search bound. Confidence for 1998–2008 is moderate: expect NSE of about 0.55–0.65 if reservoir operation does not change.
